statement: Within workplaces covered by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147, normal machine stopping does not by itself establish hazardous-energy isolation for servicing or maintenance; covered work requires control of unexpected energization, startup, or release of stored energy, while agriculture employment is expressly excluded from this standard's scope.

review.rationale: Drafted from reviewed OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 and cross-checked against the current OSHA standard on September 15, 2026. The statement preserves the standard's servicing/maintenance focus and explicit agriculture exclusion so the course does not imply universal applicability to every cultivation workplace.
review.notes: Human occupational-safety/legal-scope review is required before promotion. Facility classification, state-plan requirements, machine-specific procedures, and other applicable standards must be determined separately.

sourceContext.contextTitle: Inspection does not expand repair authority
A stopped machine can still contain hazardous energy
A reset is not a repair
Use evidence to choose the next safe action
